title: Unique Task Scheduling Order
statement: A build pipeline has n tasks (n >= 1) labeled 0 to n - 1. You are given edges, a list of pairs [a, b] meaning task a must run before task b. It is guaranteed that the dependency graph has a unique topological order (that is, at every step of the scheduling process exactly one task is ready to run). Return that unique order as a list of task labels. If the input does not actually admit a valid complete order (a cycle is present), return an empty list.
hints: The task graph forms a DAG; think about what it means for a topological order to be forced rather than ambiguous.
Use Kahn's algorithm with a plain queue: since the problem guarantees at most one node ever has indegree 0 at a time, the queue-based order is automatically the unique correct order.
Process nodes with indegree 0 one at a time, decrementing neighbors' indegree, and append each processed node to the result; if fewer than n nodes get processed, return [].
